question: What is the primary purpose of home health care documentation?

options.A: To replace verbal communication among family members
options.B: To track physician working hours in the community
options.C: To record nursing assessments and client responses
options.D: To fulfill strict hospital billing requirements

explanation: Documentation primarily captures ongoing nursing actions and client status to guide safe care delivery. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is recording care in a domestic setting uniquely challenging?

options.A: Standard hospital charts are illegal to use in private homes
options.B: Government policy forbids electronic records outside clinics
options.C: The home environment presents dynamic and unpredictable situations
options.D: Patients refuse to let nurses write down any medical details

explanation: Uncontrolled home settings require nurses to adapt documentation to fluid, real-world events. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which regulatory body sets the professional documentation standards for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN regulates nursing practice and professional conduct across the country. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h2)

question: What does contemporaneous documentation mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Summarizing a whole week of home visits on a single Friday evening
options.B: Allowing the patient to write their own notes after the nurse leaves
options.C: Writing care details as close to the time of delivery as possible
options.D: Copying old hospital records into the new home health folder

explanation: Writing entries promptly prevents memory lapses and maintains the chronological integrity of the legal record. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which component of the home health record tracks actual drug intake?
explanation: The medication sheet specifically monitors prescribed regimens and whether the client actually takes them. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why is including a local landmark in the demographic section important?

options.A: Insurance companies require GPS coordinates for claim approvals
options.B: Physicians use it to calculate the exact distance for billing transport
options.C: It helps the government collect property taxes from the client
options.D: Home addresses in many areas lack clear house numbering systems

explanation: Descriptive landmarks ensure relief nurses or emergency teams can physically locate the home without delays. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h3)

question: A nurse visiting an elderly client notices poor compliance with a diabetic diet and extreme worry about money. What should be documented?

options.A: Both physiological blood glucose levels and financial psychosocial stressors
options.B: Only the financial complaint because lifestyle issues are non-nursing tasks
options.C: Only the blood glucose readings to keep the official record strictly medical
options.D: A note stating the client is non-compliant with standard dietary advice

explanation: Holistic documentation requires capturing both physical indicators and the underlying social factors influencing health. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which type of data represents a subjective psychosocial assessment finding?

options.A: A laboratory report showing elevated serum creatinine levels
options.B: The physical dimensions of a pressure ulcer on the sacrum
options.C: Expressed feelings of caregiver burnout from a family member
options.D: A measured body temperature of thirty-eight point five degrees

explanation: Subjective psychosocial data includes emotional expressions, coping styles, and family support dynamics reported by individuals. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why must a home health care plan involve the client and family?

options.A: Nigerian law prohibits nurses from writing care plans without family consent
options.B: Clients write the final professional nursing diagnosis independently
options.C: They are responsible for carrying out most daily interventions between visits
options.D: It legally transfers all liability for adverse outcomes to the household

explanation: Because care happens outside the hospital, family members act as primary caregivers and must understand the plan. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is wrong with writing the phrase 'routine care given' in a progress note?

options.A: It breaks hospital confidentiality rules regarding home addresses
options.B: It indicates that the nurse visited the client outside permitted hours
options.C: It is too long and wastes valuable space in paper client folders
options.D: It is too vague and lacks specific details about the actions performed

explanation: Professional notes require precise descriptions of exact nursing actions rather than generalized catchphrases. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h5)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?
explanation: SBAR is a standardized communication tool used to share critical patient information concisely. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why must a nurse document a telephone conversation with a physician regarding a client?

options.A: To prove to the family that the doctor is working overtime hours
options.B: To calculate the total cost of phone credit used during the shift
options.C: To maintain an accurate legal record of verbal orders given from a distance
options.D: To comply with insurance requirements for buying foreign medicines

explanation: Documenting phone orders protects both the nurse and physician by creating a clear paper trail of remote instructions. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which challenge is commonly managed by using durable physical folders in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Strict government bans on using handwritten paper notes
options.B: Excessive availability of high-speed computer terminals
options.C: Instantaneous digital syncing with international databases
options.D: Lack of reliable electricity and internet connectivity

explanation: Paper systems remain essential when power cuts and missing digital infrastructure prevent electronic charting. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is a key risk associated with relying solely on paper home health records?

options.A: Automatic deletion of historical files due to software glitches
options.B: Unauthorized hackers accessing records through local Wi-Fi routers
options.C: Instant conversion of handwritten text into incorrect languages
options.D: Physical damage from humidity, tearing, or loss in the household

explanation: Paper documents are vulnerable to environmental wear, spills, and accidental destruction in domestic settings. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary legal implication of the phrase 'if it was not charted, it was not done'?

options.A: Physicians are legally responsible for writing all nursing interventions
options.B: Unwritten notes can be added ten years after a lawsuit concludes
options.C: Paper charts carry more legal weight than electronic database logs
options.D: Unrecorded nursing care is legally presumed never to have occurred

explanation: Courts rely on physical records as proof of care; absent notes imply the action was omitted. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h8)

question: What is the main objective of conducting regular nursing documentation audits?

options.A: To punish nurses who write longer progress notes than required
options.B: To increase the financial taxes paid by home care agencies
options.C: To identify care gaps and ensure compliance with clinical standards
options.D: To reduce the number of home visits assigned to junior staff

explanation: Audits review records systematically to improve institutional care quality and catch documentation errors early. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h8)
